reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) does not address multilayer coatings, interfacial dislocation barriers, or comparative creep behavior. E1 discusses oxidation and phase transitions in a single-composition AlCoCrFeNi coating, while E2 reports nanoindentation creep of bulk AlxCr0.2NbTiV alloys without multilayer architecture. None of the key premises are supported by the cited passages.
premises: Multilayer HEA coatings can be fabricated with alternating layers of closely related compositions and lattice mismatch
Interfaces between layers act as barriers to dislocation glide and climb
Dislocation pile-ups at interfaces reduce effective creep strain rate
Homogeneous single-phase HEA coatings serve as a valid baseline for comparison
Dislocation-mediated creep is the dominant mechanism near 1000 °C in these alloys
